title: Take Five: Six months of war
summary:
Aug 21 (Reuters) - The world's top central bank chiefs gather in Jackson Hole this week against a jittery backdrop, half a year into the Iran war and with bond markets rattled by a selloff in long-dated U.S. debt that prompted U.S. Treasury intervention.
As the gathering kicks off on Thursday, bringing together central bank chiefs from around the world, the audience for his remarks could hardly be more influential.
Brent is headed for a second straight weekly gain and its sixth advance in eight weeks, but it's the surge in refined products ⁠that is drawing growing attention as the Northern Hemisphere heads towards the colder months.
European diesel prices have jumped more than 70% since the outbreak of war in February; U.S. gasoline is up 60%.
With refining output curtailed in the Middle East, Russia, East Asia and beyond, energy-driven inflation looks here to stay.

title: China's biggest apps are inviting the West closer into its insular internet economy
summary:
For decades, China's internet economy has been a gated-off party.
While China has long since invited foreign businesses to set up shop within its borders, its internet has been closed off.
Because China's digital payment ecosystem is integrated into these social media apps, payment in the country is a challenge for foreigners, too.
But recent developments have pointed to a trend of China finally opening its doors and letting foreigners take small steps into its internet economy.
Weixin, also known as WeChat, is owned by the Chinese tech conglomerate Tencent.

title: Divorce, smartphones and control - BBC sees how Taliban run Afghanistan
summary:
Governor Abdullah Sarhadi gives money to treat a boy's broken arm and hands out funds for a local mosque - then, in his office in northern Afghanistan, an astonishing exchange unfolds.
A young woman tells the grey-bearded former Taliban commander that she wants to divorce her husband, who she accuses of months of abuse and beatings.
"If there was any chance to live together, I wouldn't be here… I have taken my decision," she says.
After trying to persuade her to avoid divorce, the governor later comments that women are "mindless" and "deficient in intellect", to laughter from the male officials, bodyguards and elders around him.
The moment gives a rare glimpse into the day-to-day realities of the Taliban's rule, five years after they swept aside the US-backed government in 2021.

title: Six months into Iran war, almost half of global oil flows from war zones
summary:
Six months ago, U.S. ‌and Israeli attacks on Iran triggered what has become the largest oil supply crisis on record, with no clear ​end in sight.
Not all of this year's supply disruptions happened at the same time.
With Saudi Arabia ​re-routing ​oil to the Red Sea and Gulf exporters ​sneaking oil secretly out of the ‌Strait of Hormuz, the current Gulf oil disruption stands at around 5 million to 7 million bpd, according to analysts' estimates.
The conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine have also cut global refining capacity by about a tenth.
Russia is ​grappling with fuel shortages and has ​banned gasoline and diesel exports, tightening global fuel markets.

title: UK, Ukraine sign AI defence partnership linked to battlefield technology
summary:
LONDON, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Britain said on Monday it had signed a partnership with Ukraine to jointly develop artificial intelligence tools ‌for defence and security, giving British researchers access to a Ukrainian ‌battlefield data platform used to train military AI systems.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Volodymyr ​Zelenskiy signed the agreement in Kyiv, making Britain the first international partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs, a government statement said.
Avengers Labs was built around an annotated dataset of 5 million battlefield images, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said earlier ‌in August, largely drawn from ⁠the military's DELTA combat system – a domestically developed battlefield management and situational-awareness system.
Advertisement AdvertisementThe platform uses data collected from cameras ⁠and sensors across Ukraine's battlefield, including information on tanks, artillery systems, drones and other military targets.
The British government said the partnership would ​initially focus on defence and national security projects ​bringing together researchers, engineers, technology ​companies and military experts from both countries.

title: Zelensky should be asked what he knew about government corruption, ex-minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells BBC
summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky should be asked questions about corruption in his government, his sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has told the BBC.
Fedorov, a popular minister who modernised the military and pioneered drone warfare, was fired last month after reportedly falling out with the head of Ukraine's armed forces.
He told the BBC that a money laundering investigation announced last week meant Zelensky should be asked about his awareness of potential corruption within his inner circle.
If I cannot share my ideas and be open about them with my own society, then what are we fighting for?"

summary:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says the door for diplomacy with Israel is open, urging it to seize a “historic opportunity”.

summary:
Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Mideast war and annexed it in 1981.
In 2019, Trump recognized Israeli sovereignty over the territory, reversing decades of U.S. policy.

title: Syria, Israel hold US-mediated talks in Jordan to de-escalate tensions
summary:
Syria’s foreign minister meets with an Israeli delegation led by the chief of the Mossad to de-escalate tensions after an Israeli strike near the Turkish border.
Syria’s Sana news agency, citing a diplomatic source, said the talks were mediated by the United States and involved a “high-level Israeli delegation”.
They also discussed efforts to ease tensions between Israel and Turkiye and to prevent their rivalry from spilling onto Syrian ‌territory, Sana reported.
Israel’s ‘red lines’Israeli media reported that the talks were “positive” and said Israeli officials had adopted a number of red lines going into talks.

title: US envoy Tom Barrack retracts comment that Syria’s Golan is occupied
summary:
Share US envoy Tom Barrack retracts comment that Syria’s Golan is occupied on social mediaUnited States Ambassador Tom Barrack has reasserted Washington’s position that Syria’s Golan Heights belongs to Israel after saying last week that the territory is occupied against “all of the international order”.
US President Donald Trump’s ambassador to Turkiye and envoy for Syria walked back that comment on Sunday, underscoring Trump’s policy of recognising Israel’s claimed sovereignty over the stretch of land in southern Syria.
Until Trump backed the Israeli claim to the Syrian territory, no country had recognised the Golan as part of Israel.
In an interview with podcaster Mario Nawfal on Friday, Barrack appeared to acknowledge that the Golan is occupied Syrian land.
Advertisement“Saying that, in the Golan with Syria, they still occupy the Golan against the UN resolutions, against all of the international order, which has said the Golan is Syria’s,” Barrack said.

title: US removes Syria from ‘state sponsor of terrorism’ list
summary:
Syria hails US’s ‘historic decision’ and says it will help the country rebuild after 14 years of civil war.
The United States has removed Syria from its list of “State Sponsors of Terrorism”, a decision Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa hailed as “historic” and said would help the country’s recovery after 14 years of civil war.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement that the action was “taken in recognition of the positive actions taken and further commitments” by al-Sharaa to “fully distance Syria from acts of international terrorism”.
Syria had been on the list since 1979, when Washington accused the government of former President Hafez al-Assad of supporting armed groups.
It had remained a major deterrent for banks and investors even after Washington dismantled its broader sanctions programme on Syria.
